Tidy and glance methods for causal results

tidy.lcc_result.Rd

tidy() returns one row per latent class (lcc_result: the effect \(\Delta_k\) and the potential-outcome class probabilities) or one row per estimand (intervention_result: \(E[Y^{g_1}]\), \(E[Y^{g_0}]\) and the effect), with broom-style columns. glance() returns a one-row summary (sample size, estimator, overlap diagnostics). as.data.frame() is tidy().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'lcc_result'
tidy(x, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95, se = c("robust", "fixed"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'intervention_result'
tidy(x, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lcc_result'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'intervention_result'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lcc_result'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'intervention_result'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

x

A result of intervene_membership() (lcc_result) or intervene_effect() (intervention_result).

conf.int

Logical; include confidence limits.

conf.level

Confidence level.

se

For lcc_result: "robust" (influence function including the measurement model; default) or "fixed" (measurement model treated as known).

...

Passed on to tidy() by as.data.frame(); ignored otherwise.

row.names, optional

Ignored (for compatibility with as.data.frame()).

Value

A data frame.

tidy.lcc_result(): columns term ("Class k"), class, estimate (\(\Delta_k\)), std.error, statistic (z), p.value, conf.low, conf.high (if conf.int), psi1, psi1.std.error, psi0, psi0.std.error.

tidy.intervention_result(): rows psi1, psi0, effect with columns term, intervention, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value, conf.low, conf.high.

glance.lcc_result(): nobs, K, estimator, folds, treatment, n_confounders, entropy, propensity.min, propensity.max, pseudo.min, pseudo.max.

glance.intervention_result(): nobs, n_dropped, estimator, family, folds, outcome, intervene, g1, g0, min_pi, max_weight.

Details

Tests and confidence intervals are Wald-type, based on the normal approximation. For intervention_result, the rows for \(E[Y^{g_1}]\) and \(E[Y^{g_0}]\) have no test statistic or p-value (a test of a mean against zero is not meaningful). The generics tidy() and glance() are re-exported from generics, so they work with broom loaded or not.

See also

intervene_membership(), intervene_effect(), causal_table()

Examples

data(programme)
# \donttest{
# effect of the school programme on the latent wellbeing classes, as tidy tables
# measurement model of the eight follow-up wellbeing items only (no treatment, no covariates)
m <- latentmixtures::lca(programme, low_mood:friends, K = 3)   # Flourishing, Moderate, Distressed
#> Starting Julia ...
r <- intervene_membership(m, programme, treatment = programme,
                confounders = c(female, age, low_ses, distress, belonging))
tidy(r, conf.level = 0.9)   # 90 percent intervals
#>      term class    estimate  std.error statistic      p.value   conf.low
#> 1 Class 1     1  0.19623314 0.03068359  6.395377 1.601515e-10  0.1457631
#> 2 Class 2     2 -0.05540049 0.03649414 -1.518065 1.289980e-01 -0.1154280
#> 3 Class 3     3 -0.14083265 0.02153219 -6.540563 6.128785e-11 -0.1762500
#>      conf.high      psi1 psi1.std.error      psi0 psi0.std.error
#> 1  0.246703162 0.6263778     0.04041572 0.4301447     0.03583990
#> 2  0.004627035 0.2379277     0.03644535 0.2933282     0.03081426
#> 3 -0.105415349 0.1356945     0.01681772 0.2765271     0.02444146
tidy(r, se = "fixed")       # SEs treating the measurement model as known (smaller)
#>      term class    estimate  std.error statistic      p.value   conf.low
#> 1 Class 1     1  0.19623314 0.03054539  6.424314 1.324655e-10  0.1363653
#> 2 Class 2     2 -0.05540049 0.03569695 -1.551967 1.206702e-01 -0.1253652
#> 3 Class 3     3 -0.14083265 0.02056606 -6.847819 7.498423e-12 -0.1811414
#>     conf.high      psi1 psi1.std.error      psi0 psi0.std.error
#> 1  0.25610100 0.6263778     0.04041572 0.4301447     0.03583990
#> 2  0.01456426 0.2379277     0.03644535 0.2933282     0.03081426
#> 3 -0.10052392 0.1356945     0.01681772 0.2765271     0.02444146
glance(r)
#>   nobs K estimator folds treatment n_confounders  entropy propensity.min
#> 1 2000 3      aipw     5 programme             5 0.665586     0.01904342
#>   propensity.max pseudo.min pseudo.max
#> 1      0.9228678 -0.3859328   1.526334
# }
